blocks.content: The decision of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly on whether a bill is a Money Bill or not shall be final.

rows: Elected by members of the Assembly
Elected by members of the Council
Final authority to decide if a bill is a Money Bill
Has no authority or power over Money Bills
Elected from Council members (Not an ex-officio officer)
Decides anti-defection cases for Assembly members
Decides anti-defection cases for Council members

items: Unlike Parliament, there is no constitutional provision for a joint sitting of both Houses of the State Legislature.
Questions regarding disqualification of members under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) are determined by the Presiding Officer of the respective House.
The Chairman of the Legislative Council cannot preside while a resolution for his removal is under consideration, though he has the right to speak and take part in proceedings.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker are elected by the Legislative Assembly from amongst its members.
The Speaker decides whether a bill is a Money Bill or not, and this decision is final.
Unlike the Vice-President in Rajya Sabha, the Chairman of the Legislative Council is elected from amongst the members of the Council itself.
The salaries and allowances of the Presiding Officers are fixed by the State Legislature and charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Presiding officers do not vote in the first instance, but exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.
